clue.text: Cat finally spots litter

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the last letter of cat
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A cat eventually notices its litter tray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb meaning sees, but it is a noun: an outbreak of pimples.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter and trash are synonyms for rubbish strewn about.

clue.text: Deal mostly involving one secret society

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is wrapped around the other
mostly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to deal is to trade
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A shady deal that brings in a single secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: TRADE loses its last letter to give TRAD, which then takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a Chinese criminal secret society, a kind of organised gang.

clue.text: Piece in paper, tiny piece with no heading

indicators.note: having no heading means the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a particle is a minute fragment

explanation.surface: A small newspaper item that has been printed without a headline.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTICLE without its first letter P gives the answer; 'heading' plays on newspaper headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a written item published in a newspaper.

clue.text: Holidaying initially at Kew, we read her new historical novel

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into a fresh arrangement
initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of holidaying
taken as written

explanation.surface: On holiday at Kew Gardens, someone reads her a recently published historical novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is a London district famous for its botanic gardens. Hereward the Wake is Charles Kingsley's novel about an English rebel against the Normans.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward the Wake (1866) is a novel set in the eleventh century, so it is historical fiction.

clue.text: Hospital doctor in charge leaving confused geriatrics at end of corridor

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up and need rearranging
leaving means going out of, so those letters are removed from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of corridor

explanation.surface: A senior doctor leaves bewildered elderly patients at the end of a hospital corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: GERIATRICS minus IC leaves GERIATRS, which is rearranged and followed by R.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor below consultant, in specialist training.

clue.text: Hint about a rest

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a hint can be a reminder or prompt
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone ought to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is what is left over, its remainder.

clue.text: Visitor in front of entrance, caught by sudden blast of wind

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

parts.note: a gust is a brief strong rush of wind

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of entrance

explanation.surface: A visitor standing at the front door is hit by a sudden blast of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is someone invited to visit a home or event.

clue.text: Psychiatrist with one northern g-girl, very shy type

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for northern
the stuttered letter taken as written
Violet is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist with a stammering northern girl who is extremely shy.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter in 'g-girl' is not just colour: it supplies the G before the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrinking violet is an idiom for an extremely timid, retiring person.

clue.text: Went round gallery surrounded by staff

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a rod is a staff or pole
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone toured an art gallery while flanked by its employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests gallery employees, but here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rotated is to have turned or spun round.

clue.text: Meet up again with English prisoner, never changing outwardly

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the rearranged word sits around the other pieces
changing means the letters of the word are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English
con is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: Arranging a reunion with an English prisoner whose appearance never alters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' applies to the rearranged word: it splits after its first letter to take the English prisoner inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconvene is to assemble again after a break.

clue.text: Temporary home — get word about one

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a term is a word or expression
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in temporary housing is waiting to hear news about one person.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes an arrangement lasting only for the meantime, provisional.

clue.text: Wandering, boy round desert

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the first word goes around the second

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
to rat is to desert or betray

explanation.surface: A boy wandering around the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a sandy noun; it is the verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and straying from a steady course, as a wandering path does.

clue.text: Wicked witch and king don't, swallowing it in pantomime

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside
wicked suggests something twisted and corrupted, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wicked witches and kings refrain from swallowing anything in a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked witch' reads as a stock pantomime villain, but 'Wicked' is the anagram signal. A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show based on a folk tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Whittington is the hero of a classic British pantomime, the poor boy who becomes Lord Mayor of London.

clue.text: Watches Communist and becomes very angry

parts.note: to watch is to see
Red is a common label for a Communist

explanation.surface: Someone watches a Communist and flies into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is an idiom for losing one's temper.

clue.text: Foreign girl has an earthly paradise

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl from abroad has found heaven on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La, from James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, is a byword for an idyllic hidden utopia.

clue.text: Good sieve, cooking utensil

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a riddle is a coarse sieve for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: A list of kitchen equipment: a good sieve and a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDDLE here is not a puzzle but a large garden sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron plate used for cooking over heat.

clue.text: Marvellous, small company at making what a soldier might wear

parts.note: great means marvellous
Co is the short form of company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wonderful little firm is producing military clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A greatcoat is a heavy overcoat, standard military winter issue.

clue.text: Rarebit cooked for a judge

indicators.note: cooked means altered by preparation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Welsh rarebit prepared for a judge to taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle a dispute, a judge.

clue.text: Boy cut a long sizzling sausage

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: sizzling suggests being agitated in a hot pan, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy slices a lengthy sausage that is frying in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: A bologna is a large smoked sausage named after the Italian city.

clue.text: Fencer's warning in area of kitchen garden

indicators.note: in the area of means located within the words that follow

parts.note: found inside kitchen garden

explanation.surface: A fencer calls a warning while standing in a vegetable plot.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the French call fencers use to tell an opponent to take a guard position.

clue.text: Change back

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to turn something the other way round
second meaning: to go backwards, as a car does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Change back' reads as one instruction to undo something; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse is both to invert a decision and to drive a vehicle backwards.

clue.text: Superb fetching animal?

parts.note: surface reading: a gorgeous, attractive creature
setter's reading: an excellent beast that fetches things, a gun dog bringing back game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' reads as attractive, but it means bringing back; 'superb' stands for a word meaning first-rate that is also a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of gun dog is bred to bring back shot birds, and its coat is a rich yellow.

clue.text: On day before festival calls for US actor

parts.note: re means on or concerning
an eve is the day before a festival, as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: On the day before a holiday, an American actor is in demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Reeve was the American film actor best known as Superman.

clue.text: Send for terms of reference

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to transmit money or refer a case on
second meaning: the scope of authority given to a body

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as sending off for a document; the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to send payment; as a noun it is the defined area of a committee's responsibility.

clue.text: Angry about no good unappreciative type

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

parts.note: irate means angry
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a worthless, thankless person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is a person who shows no gratitude.

clue.text: One in old spirit container

indicators.note: in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A single bottle of aged liquor in a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil drum is a large cylindrical metal barrel for storing liquids.

clue.text: Degradation in a cellar

parts.note: taken as written
a basement is a cellar

explanation.surface: Someone suffers humiliation by being kept down in a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is humiliation, a lowering of someone's dignity.

clue.text: Shout for minister?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for buying a round, as in 'my shout'
second meaning: to minister to a patient, give medical care

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests yelling for a clergyman or politician, but 'shout' is the British idea of paying for everyone's drinks, and 'minister' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is something paid for on someone's behalf, and to treat a patient is to tend them.
